parole.significato: Combines with an (often clipped) word to create a noun referring to a person with a related property. Gives a familiar…
parole.testo: * Possibly from Tavringer Romani -o, a masculine ending for nouns, cf. buro (“non-Traveller, farmer”), bölo (“bull”). Compare Icelandic -ó.
Via Månsing cant borrowed from Tavringer Romani bassj, bassjt, derived from Romani berś. Cognate to Sanskrit वर्ष (varṣa, “year”).

parole.significato: to sell (usually illicit drugs or stolen goods), to peddle
parole.testo: From Tavringer Romani bickna, bäckna (“to sell”), from Romani bikinel (“to sell”). and to Hindi बेचना (becnā, “sell”). Related to Sanskrit विक्रीणाति (vikrīṇāti, “to sell”) and Pali vikkiṇāti (“he sells”).
From Tavringer Romani beng, bäng (“devil, satan”), from Romani beng (“devil”). Related to Sanskrit व्यङ्ग (vyaṅga, “speckled, deformed”).
From Tavringer Romani dinalo, dingalo (“crazy”), from Romani dinelo (“stupid, crazy”). Related to Sanskrit दीन (dīna, “weak”).
From Tavringer Romani gola (“shout, scream”). Attested since the late 1960s.

parole.significato: to understand, to follow, to get
parole.testo: From Tavringer Romani haja, from Romani haj- (“to understand”), further origin obscure.
From Tavringer Romani hispa (“small house, cottage”), probably a borrowing from Slovene jìspa (“small house, cottage”) or some other Slavic language. Compare also Rodi Norwegian hispa.

parole.significato: experiencing a fit of anxiety or prone to experiencing fits of anxiety, "hysterical"
parole.testo: From hispa (“mental asylum”) + -ig (“-y”), from Tavringer Romani hispa (“small house, cottage”), probably a borrowing from Slovene jìspa (“small house, cottage”) or some other Slavic language.
From Tavringer Romani jakk (“eye”), from Romani jakh (“eye”). Related to Sanskrit अक्षि (akṣi, “eye”). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ókʷs (“eye”). Doublet of öga.

parole.significato: to talk with more or less meaningless content
parole.testo: From an older slang sense ’to live’, from Tavringer Romani jida, jiddra (“to live”), cf. jidrepa (“life”), from Romani džiw- (“to live”). Related to Sanskrit जीवति (jīvati, “to live”).
From Tavringer Romani jucklo, jycklo (“dog”), from Romani ʒukel, from Sanskrit जकुट (jakuṭa, “dog”).

parole.significato: to win, to procure (as a prize)
parole.testo: Could possibly be from an older slang sense of kamma meaning ’to get, to earn’, from Tavringer Romani kamma (“to have, to own”), compare kamma noll (“to get nothing”), from Romani kam- (“to wish, to request”). Related to Sanskrit कामयति (kāmayati, “to wish, to desire”), from *keh₂- (“to desire, wish

Said to be a metaphor for combing lice out of hair without success. Could also possibly be from an older slang sense ’to get, to earn’, from Tavringer Romani kamma (“to have, to own”), compare kamma hem (“to win, to procure”), from Romani kam- (“to wish, to request”). Related to Sanskrit कामयति (kām

parole.significato: to fix, to arrange, to pull something off
parole.testo: From Tavringer Romani kera, kira (“to do, to work”), from Romani ker- (“to do”). Same root as in Sanskrit करोति (karoti, “to do”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kʷer- (“to do, make”).

parole.significato: a cant or secret language (especially formerly) used by chimneysweeps
parole.testo: From an older chimneysweep slang word knopare (“chimneysweep”) + moj, from Tavringer Romani muj, måj, möj, måjj (“mouth”), from Romani mui (“mouth”), compare English mooey (“mouth, face”). Related to Sanskrit मुख (mukha, “mouth, face”).

parole.significato: a fight, a scrimmage, a scuffle
parole.testo: From Tavringer Romani kura (“to hit, to punch”), from Romani kur- (“to hit, to beat, to fight”). Related to Sanskrit कुट्टयति (kuṭṭayati, “to pound, to strike”).

From Tavringer Romani ladjas, lajjas, lajvas (“be ashamed”), from Romani ladž (“shame”). Related to Sanskrit लज्जा (lajjā, “shame”), Hindi लाज (lāj, “shame”). Related to laja (“have fun”), from Tavringer Romani ladjas, lajjas, lajvas (“be ashamed”), from Romani ladž (“shame”). Related to Sanskrit लज्जा (lajjā, “shame”), Hindi लाज (lāj, “shame”). The shift in meaning from ’be ashamed’ to ’have fun’ is probably due to influence from another Romani loan latt

parole.significato: to play, to have fun, to mess around, to joke
parole.testo: From lattjo + -a, from Tavringer Romani lattjo (“good, fine”), Romani laćho (“good”), same root as in Sanskrit लक्ष्मी (lakṣmī, “good fortune, wealth”).
From Tavringer Romani lattjo (“good, fine”), Romani laćho (“good”), same root as in Sanskrit लक्ष्मी (lakṣmī, “good fortune, wealth”). Compare Rodi Norwegian lakjo.
From Tavringer Romani lover, loviar (“money”), from Romani lowo (“coin”). Related to Sanskrit लोहवर (lohavara, “gold”).

parole.significato: an (open-face) sandwich (slice(s) of bread with toppings, usually buttered)
parole.testo: Attested since 1910, of uncertain origin with at least two proposed etymologies: * From a dialectal verb macka (“to work, to finish”), related to German machen (“to make”). * From Tavringer Romani macka (“to grease, to cream, to butter”), from Romani mak (“grease, lubricant”). Related to Sanskrit म्
From Tavringer Romani mander, mandro (“I, me”), cf. manders (“my”). Originally a frozen ablative of Romani me (“I, me”), compare Sanskrit माम् (mām, “me”).
From Tavringer Romani muck (“free”), from Romani muk- (“to let, to release, to leave”). Related to Sanskrit मुञ्चति (muñcati, “to release, to free, to let go”).

parole.significato: to finish one’s time in military training; to be relieved from a time in conscription
parole.testo: From Tavringer Romani mucka (“to release, be released”), from Tavringer Romani muck (“free”), from Romani muk- (“to let, to release, to leave”). Related to Sanskrit मुञ्चति (muñcati, “to release, to free, to let go”).

parole.significato: to travel around and sell transportable goods
parole.testo: From månsing cant, of uncertain origin, possibly: * From Tavringer Romani nasja (“to walk, run”), from Romani naš- (“to run, hurry, flee”). * From a dialectal word nasa (”to smell, to search”).
From Tavringer Romani noba, nåbba, from German Rotwelsch nobis (“nothing”), of uncertain origin.
Back-formation from paja (“to break”), from Tavringer Romani pagra, paggra (“to break, to destroy”), from Romani phag- (“to break, to destroy”); compare Sanskrit भग्न (bhagná, “broken”).

parole.significato: to stop working, to become broken
parole.testo: From Tavringer Romani pagra, paggra (“to break, to destroy”), from Romani phag- (“to break, to destroy”). Related to Sanskrit भनक्ति (bhanakti, “to break”).

From Tavringer Romani pavli, pavali, pava, pavani (“bottle”), cognate to Traveller Norwegian pavvali, pavvani (“bottle”). Nominalization of Romani pi- (“to drink”), with an infinitive suffix -va found in other Romani varieties (but not in Scandoromani), e.g. Kalo Finnish Romani piāvā (“to drink”).
From pröjsa (“to pay”). From Tavringer Romani prejsa, from Romani pleiservāva-.

parole.significato: to pay; to give money in exchange for goods or services
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tavringer Romani prejsa, from Romani pleiservāva-. Related to Traveller Norwegian preisa, pressa and Kalo Finnish Romani presavā. Perhaps a loan from a Slavic language, e.g. Serbo-Croatian plaćati. The initial pr- as opposed to pl-, indicates however that it was influenced or borrowed
From Tavringer Romani sjucker, sjycker (“beautiful, pretty”), from Romani śukar (“beautiful, amiable, pleasant”). Related to Sanskrit शुक्र (śukra, “light, white, pure”).
Possibly from Tavringer Romani sivava (“to sow”). First attested in 1934.
From Tavringer Romani syrak (“stingy, cheap”).
From Tavringer Romani tjavo (“boy”), from Romani ćhavo. Compare Rodi Norwegian kjavo.
From Tavringer Romani [Term?], from Romani [Term?]. Compare origin of schackra.

parole.significato: to inform on, to snitch; often to someone of authority, such as the police
parole.testo: From Tavringer Romani tjalla (“inform on”), probably from Romani xalo (“fraud, impostor, non-Romani”). Related to Sanskrit छलिन् (chalin, “cheat, swindler, fraud”).

Attested since 1851. From Tavringer Romani tjej, from Romani ćhaj (“girl”), a feminine form of ćhavo (“boy”). Derived from the root found in the Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀙𑀸𑀯 (chāva), corresponding to Pali chāpa (“the young of an animal”).
From Tavringer Romani tji (“not, nothing, no”), related to Traveller Norwegian kji (“not, nothing, no”), from Romani či (“not, nothing”). Probably a borrowing from Armenian չի (čʻi, “not, no”).
From Tavringer Romani tjuro, tjuring, from Romani ćhuri, cognate to Sanskrit छुरी (churī, “knife”).
From Tavringer Romani vissj, vässj (“forest”), from Romani veś (“forest”), a borrowing from Mazanderani ویشه (višé, “forest”), compare Persian بیشه (biše, “forest”).
